about: A top of descent on a leg that flies more than its line at its end (the engine's navlog_with_descents): the planner adds a procedure's miles more (a traffic pattern to land, AIM 4-3-3 and AC 90-66C 11.2-11.3; an arrival or an approach) and a hold at the destination to the leg's ete_min and fuel_gal before the descent is placed, and those are flown after the top of descent, so its minutes and gallons are the line's to it alone. A hold at a stop is flown at the leg's start, before it. One 60 nm leg at 100 kt over the ground, 8 gal/h, 5,500 ft down to a 1,500 ft pattern: 4,000 ft at three to one (333 ft a nm, AIM 2-1-2's 3 degree path) is 12 nm, finished where the 45-degree entry begins, 1.7236 nm out, so the top is 60 - 13.7236 = 46.2764 nm along (46.3), 46.2764 x 0.6 = 27.77 min (27.8) and 46.2764 / 100 x 8 = 3.70 gal. Each case's ete_min and fuel_gal are the line's 36 min and 4.8 gal plus what it adds. Worked by hand, not from the code. Engine: engine/facade/tests/tod_after_leg_end.rs. Not the web's: the planner's nav log asks this rule.

cases.name: No procedure: the top of descent's minutes are its miles at the ground speed
A pattern to land, 3.0 nm more, 1.8 min and 0.24 gal at the leg's end: after the top of descent
A hold at the destination, 4.0 min and 0.53 gal at the leg's end: after the top of descent
A hold at the leg's start (a stop's, at_end false): before the top of descent
